verses.zh: 你这论断人的，无论你是谁，也无可推诿。你在甚么事上论断人，就在甚么事上定自己的罪；因你这论断人的，自己所行却和别人一样。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Therefore[NOTE:2] you are without excuse,[NOTE:3] whoever you are,[NOTE:4] when you judge someone else.[NOTE:5] For on whatever grounds[NOTE:6] you judge another, you condemn yourself, because you who judge practice the same things.
notes: Rom 2:1-29 presents unusual difficulties for the interpreter. There have been several major approaches to the chapter and the group(s) it refers to: (1) Rom 2:14 refers to Gentile Christians, not Gentiles who obey the Jewish law. (2) Paul in Rom 2 is presenting a hypothetical viewpoint: If anyone could obey the law, that person would be justified, but no one can. (3) The reference to “the ones who do the law” in 2:13 are those who “do” the law in the right way, on the basis of faith, not according to Jewish legalism. (4) Rom 2:13 only speaks about Christians being judged in the future, along with such texts as Rom 14:10 and 2 Cor 5:10. (5) Paul’s material in Rom 2 is drawn heavily from Diaspora Judaism, so that the treatment of the law presented here cannot be harmonized with other things Paul says about the law elsewhere (E. P. Sanders, Paul, the Law, and the Jewish People, 123); another who sees Rom 2 as an example of Paul’s inconsistency in his treatment of the law is H. Räisänen, Paul and the Law [WUNT], 101-9. (6) The list of blessings and curses in Deut 27-30 provide the background for Rom 2; the Gentiles of 2:14 are Gentile Christians, but the condemnation of Jews in 2:17-24 addresses the failure of Jews as a nation to keep the law as a whole (A. Ito, “Romans 2: A Deuteronomistic Reading,” JSNT 59 [1995]: 21-37).
Some interpreters (e.g., C. K. Barrett, Romans [HNTC], 43) connect the inferential Διό (dio, “therefore”) with 1:32a, treating 1:32b as a parenthetical comment by Paul.
That is, “you have nothing to say in your own defense” (so translated by TCNT).
Grk “O man.”
Grk “Therefore, you are without excuse, O man, everyone [of you] who judges.”
Grk “in/by (that) which.”

verses.zh: 我们知道这样行的人，　神必照真理审判他。
verses.en: Now we know that God’s judgment is in accordance with truth[NOTE:1] against those who practice such things.
notes: Or “based on truth.”

verses.zh: 你这人哪，你论断行这样事的人，自己所行的却和别人一样，你以为能逃脱　神的审判吗？
verses.en: And do you think,[NOTE:1] whoever you are, when you judge[NOTE:2] those who practice such things and yet do them yourself,[NOTE:3] that you will escape God’s judgment?
notes: Grk “do you think this,” referring to the clause in v. 3b.
Grk “O man, the one who judges.”
Grk “and do them.” The other words are supplied to bring out the contrast implied in this clause.

verses.zh: 还是你藐视他丰富的恩慈、宽容、忍耐，不晓得他的恩慈是领你悔改呢？
verses.en: Or do you have contempt for the wealth of his kindness, forbearance, and patience, and yet do not know[NOTE:1] that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
notes: Grk “being unaware.”

verses.zh: 你竟任着你刚硬不悔改的心，为自己积蓄忿怒，以致　神震怒，显他公义审判的日子来到。
verses.en: But because of your stubbornness[NOTE:1] and your unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourselves in the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment is revealed![NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “hardness.” Concerning this imagery, see Jer 4:4; Ezek 3:7; 1 En. 16:3.
Grk “in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God.”

verses.zh: 他必照各人的行为报应各人。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] will reward[NOTE:2] each one according to his works:[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “who.” The relative pronoun was converted to a personal pronoun and, because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Or “will render,” “will recompense.” In this context Paul is setting up a hypothetical situation, not stating that salvation is by works.
A quotation from Ps 62:12; Prov 24:12; a close approximation to Matt 16:27.

verses.zh: 凡恒心行善、寻求荣耀、尊贵和不能朽坏之福的，就以永生报应他们；
verses.en: eternal life to those who by perseverance in good works seek glory and honor and immortality,

verses.zh: 惟有结党、不顺从真理、反顺从不义的，就以忿怒、恼恨报应他们；
verses.en: but[NOTE:1] wrath and anger to those who live in selfish ambition[NOTE:2] and do not obey the truth but follow[NOTE:3] unrighteousness.
notes: This contrast is clearer and stronger in Greek than can be easily expressed in English.
Grk “those who [are] from selfish ambition.”
Grk “are persuaded by, obey.”

verses.zh: 将患难、困苦加给一切作恶的人，先是犹太人，后是希腊人，
verses.en: There will be[NOTE:1] affliction and distress on everyone[NOTE:2] who does evil, on the Jew first and also the Greek,[NOTE:3]
notes: No verb is expressed in this verse, but the verb “to be” is implied by the Greek construction. Literally “suffering and distress on everyone…”
Grk “every soul of man.”
Paul uses the term Greek here and in v. 10 to refer to non-Jews, i.e., Gentiles.

verses.zh: 却将荣耀、尊贵、平安加给一切行善的人，先是犹太人，后是希腊人。
verses.en: but[NOTE:1] glory and honor and peace for everyone who does good, for the Jew first and also the Greek.
notes: Grk “but even,” to emphasize the contrast. The second word has been omitted since it is somewhat redundant in English idiom.

verses.zh: 因为　神不偏待人。
verses.en: For there is no partiality with God.

verses.zh: 凡没有律法犯了罪的，也必不按律法灭亡；凡在律法以下犯了罪的，也必按律法受审判。
verses.en: For all who have sinned apart from the law[NOTE:1] will also perish apart from the law, and all who have sinned under the law will be judged by the law.
notes: This is the first occurrence of law (nomos) in Romans. Exactly what Paul means by the term has been the subject of much scholarly debate. According to J. A. Fitzmyer (Romans [AB], 131-35; 305-6) there are at least four different senses: (1) figurative, as a “principle”; (2) generic, meaning “a law”; (3) as a reference to the OT or some part of the OT; and (4) as a reference to the Mosaic law. This last usage constitutes the majority of Paul’s references to “law” in Romans.

verses.zh: （原来在　神面前，不是听律法的为义，乃是行律法的称义。
verses.en: For it is not those who hear the law who are righteous before God, but those who do the law will be declared righteous.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Greek sentence expresses this contrast more succinctly than is possible in English. Grk “For not the hearers of the law are righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be declared righteous.”

verses.zh: 没有律法的外邦人若顺着本性行律法上的事，他们虽然没有律法，自己就是自己的律法。
verses.en: For whenever the Gentiles,[NOTE:1] who do not have the law, do by nature[NOTE:2] the things required by the law,[NOTE:3] these who do not have the law are a law to themselves.
notes: Gentile is a NT term for a non-Jew.

Some (e.g. C. E. B. Cranfield, Romans [ICC], 1:135-37) take the phrase φύσει (phusei, “by nature”) to go with the preceding “do not have the law,” thus: “the Gentiles who do not have the law by nature,” that is, by virtue of not being born Jewish.
Grk “do by nature the things of the law.”

verses.zh: 这是显出律法的功用刻在他们心里，他们是非之心同作见证，并且他们的思念互相较量，或以为是，或以为非。）
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] show that the work of the law is written[NOTE:2] in their hearts, as their conscience bears witness and their conflicting thoughts accuse or else defend[NOTE:3] them,[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “who.” The relative pronoun was converted to a personal pronoun and, because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Grk “show the work of the law [to be] written,” with the words in brackets implied by the Greek construction.
Or “excuse.”
Grk “their conscience bearing witness and between the thoughts accusing or also defending one another.”

verses.zh: 就在　神藉耶稣基督审判人隐秘事的日子，照着我的福音所言。
verses.en: on the day when God will judge[NOTE:1] the secrets of human hearts,[NOTE:2] according to my gospel[NOTE:3] through Christ Jesus.
notes: The form of the Greek word is either present or future, but it is best to translate in future because of the context of future judgment.
Grk “of people.”
On my gospel cf. Rom 16:25; 2 Tim 2:8.

verses.zh: 你称为犹太人，又倚靠律法，且指着　神夸口；
verses.en: But if you call yourself a Jew and rely on the law[NOTE:1] and boast of your relationship to God[NOTE:2]
notes: The law refers to the Mosaic law, described mainly in the OT books of Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy.
Grk “boast in God.” This may be an allusion to Jer 9:24.

verses.zh: 既从律法中受了教训，就晓得　神的旨意，也能分别是非（或译：也喜爱那美好的事）；
verses.en: and know his will[NOTE:1] and approve the superior things because you receive instruction from the law,[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “the will.”
Grk “because of being instructed out of the law.”

verses.zh: 又深信自己是给瞎子领路的，是黑暗中人的光，
verses.en: and if you are convinced[NOTE:1] that you yourself are a guide to the blind, a light to those who are in darkness,
notes: This verb is parallel to the verbs in vv. 17-18a, so it shares the conditional meaning even though the word “if” is not repeated.

verses.zh: 是蠢笨人的师傅，是小孩子的先生，在律法上有知识和真理的模范。
verses.en: an educator of the senseless, a teacher of little children, because you have in the law the essential features of knowledge and of the truth—

verses.zh: 你既是教导别人，还不教导自己吗？你讲说人不可偷窃，自己还偷窃吗？
verses.en: therefore[NOTE:1] you who teach someone else, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
notes: The structure of vv. 21-24 is difficult. Some take these verses as the apodosis of the conditional clauses (protases) in vv. 17-20; others see vv. 17-20 as an instance of anacoluthon (a broken off or incomplete construction).

verses.zh: 你说人不可奸淫，自己还奸淫吗？你厌恶偶像，自己还偷窃庙中之物吗？
verses.en: You who tell others not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor[NOTE:1] idols, do you rob temples?
notes: Or “detest.”

verses.zh: 你指着律法夸口，自己倒犯律法、玷辱　神吗？
verses.en: You who boast in the law dishonor God by transgressing the law!

verses.zh: 神的名在外邦人中，因你们受了亵渎，正如经上所记的。
verses.en: For just as it is written, “the name of God is being blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Isa 52:5.

verses.zh: 你若是行律法的，割礼固然于你有益；若是犯律法的，你的割礼就算不得割礼。
verses.en: For circumcision[NOTE:1] has its value if you practice the law, but[NOTE:2] if you break the law,[NOTE:3] your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
notes: Circumcision refers to male circumcision as prescribed in the OT, which was given as a covenant to Abraham in Gen 17:10-14. Its importance for Judaism can hardly be overstated: According to J. D. G. Dunn (Romans [WBC], 1:120) it was the “single clearest distinguishing feature of the covenant people.” J. Marcus has suggested that the terms used for circumcision (περιτομή, peritomē) and uncircumcision (ἀκροβυστία, akrobustia) were probably derogatory slogans used by Jews and Gentiles to describe their opponents (“The Circumcision and the Uncircumcision in Rome,” NTS 35 [1989]: 77-80).
This contrast is clearer and stronger in Greek than can be easily expressed in English.
Grk “if you should be a transgressor of the law.”

verses.zh: 所以那未受割礼的，若遵守律法的条例，他虽然未受割礼，岂不算是有割礼吗？
verses.en: Therefore if the uncircumcised man obeys[NOTE:1] the righteous requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?
notes: The Greek word φυλάσσω (phulassō, traditionally translated “keep”) in this context connotes preservation of and devotion to an object as well as obedience.

verses.zh: 而且那本来未受割礼的，若能全守律法，岂不是要审判你这有仪文和割礼竟犯律法的人吗？
verses.en: And the physically uncircumcised man,[NOTE:1] by keeping the law, will judge you to be the transgressor of the law, even though[NOTE:2] you have the letter[NOTE:3] and circumcision!
notes: Grk “the uncircumcision by nature.” The word “man” is supplied here to make clear that male circumcision (or uncircumcision) is in view.
Grk “through,” but here the preposition seems to mean “(along) with,” “though provided with,” as BDAG 224 s.v. διά A.3.c indicates.
Or “written code.”

verses.zh: 因为外面作犹太人的，不是真犹太人；外面肉身的割礼，也不是真割礼。
verses.en: For a person is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision something that is outward in the flesh,

verses.zh: 惟有里面作的，才是真犹太人；真割礼也是心里的，在乎灵，不在乎仪文。这人的称赞不是从人来的，乃是从　神来的。
verses.en: but someone is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is of the heart[NOTE:1] by the Spirit[NOTE:2] and not by the letter.[NOTE:3] This person’s[NOTE:4] praise is not from people but from God.
notes: On circumcision is of the heart see Lev 26:41; Deut 10:16; Jer 4:4; Ezek 44:9.
Some have taken the phrase ἐν πνεύματι (en pneumati, “by/in [the] S/spirit”) not as a reference to the Holy Spirit, but referring to circumcision as “spiritual and not literal” (RSV).
Or “written code.”
Grk “whose.” The relative pronoun has been replaced by the phrase “this person’s” and, because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started in the translation.
